name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index $4,032 per 40ft on 26 Nov, still just above the $4,000 Alert line after another weekly fall
state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,032 per 40ft container on 26 Nov, still just above the $4,000 Alert line (Drewry). Shanghai–New York fell 7% to $7,615 and Shanghai–Los Angeles 8% to $6,437, with transpacific rates down for eight straight weeks, while Shanghai–Genoa rose 8% to $4,802 and Shanghai–Rotterdam was flat at $3,485. The next assessment is due on 3 Dec; a fall of under 1% would take the index below the Alert line.
for_you: Importers and retailers shipping from Asia face container costs well above pre-crisis levels, especially to the US; these tend to feed through to shelf prices and delivery times over the following months. Rates are falling but remain at Alert level.
rubric_hit: Drewry WCI $4,032/FEU on 26 Nov > $4,000 Alert line
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
